answers.answer: সাম্রাজ্যের সামরিক ও আর্থিক সম্পদ নিঃশেষ হয়ে যায়
answers.quote: Emperor Aurangzeb had depleted the military and financial resources of his empire by fighting a long war in the Deccan.
answers.notes: Direct match to claim c01.

answers.quote: the ruler of Iran, Nadir Shah, sacked and plundered the city of Delhi in 1739 and took away immense amounts of wealth.
answers.notes: Nadir Shah sacked Delhi in 1739 per c03.

answers.quote: Nizamul-Mulk Asaf Jah, the founder of Hyderabad state (1724-1748), was one of the most powerful members at the court of the Mughal Emperor Farrukh Siyar.
answers.notes: Founder of Hyderabad state per c08/c43.

answers.quote: Murshid Kuli Khan became Governor of Bengal in 1717 under Mughal aegis but his link with Delhi was limited to sending tribute. Shuja-un-din became Nawab in 1727 and ruled till 1739 when Alivardi Khan assumed charge. In 1756 Siraj-ud-daula became the Nawab of Bengal on the death of his grandfather Alivardi Khan.
answers.notes: Murshid Quli Khan became Governor of Bengal in 1717 and Bengal broke away under him (c12/c41).

answers.quote: In 1630, Shivaji was born in the Bhonsle clan to Shahji and Jijabai.
answers.notes: CONFLICT in claims: c33 states explicitly 'In 1630, Shivaji was born' (s2), but c22 gives Shivaji's lifespan as 1627-1680 (s1), implying 1627. Answered with the explicit birth claim c33; ১৬২৭ is also defensible from c22.

answers.quote: Raigad Fort, Maharashtra, with the grand entrance to the palace where Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was crowned in 1674, marking the formal beginning of the Maratha Empire.
answers.notes: Crowned at Raigad in 1674 per c35.

answers.quote: Chauth 25 per cent of the land revenue claimed by zamindars. In the Deccan this was collected by the Marathas. Sardeshmukhi 9-10 per cent of the land revenue paid to the head revenue collector in the Deccan.
answers.notes: Chauth was 25 per cent of land revenue per c28.

answers.quote: The third battle of Panipat commenced on 14th January 1761. But the conflict and its outcome were brewing since 1752 when Maratha forces overran North India and established their influence at the Delhi court. The Marathas were not content with their acquisitions and looked greedily towards the Punjab, which was ruled by a tributary of Abdali.
answers.notes: Third battle of Panipat commenced 14 January 1761 per c49.

answers.quote: Several battles were fought by Guru Gobind Singh against the Rajput and Mughal rulers, both before and after the institution of the Khalsa in 1699.
answers.notes: Institution of the Khalsa in 1699 per c65.

answers.quote: Ranjit Singh was the son of the Sukerchakia Misl Chief, Mahan Singh. He in alliance with Sahib Singh of Gujarat and Milkha Singh of Pindiwala, attacked Shahanchi Khan and occupied Lahore in 1799. After Lahore Ranjit Singh annexed Amritsar from the Bhangis along with all their other territories. Master of Lahore and Amritsar. Ranjit Singh, laid the foundation of a sovereign Sikh monarchy in the Punjab
answers.notes: Ranjit Singh was son of the Sukerchakia misl chief per c64.

answers.quote: Nobles appointed as governors (subadars) often controlled the offices of revenue and military administration (diwani and faujdari) as well. This gave them extraordinary political, economic and military powers over vast regions of the Mughal Empire.
answers.notes: Subadars controlled diwani and faujdari per c02.

answers.quote: Ahmad Shah Abdali, who invaded north India five times between 1748 and 1761.
answers.notes: Abdali invaded five times 1748-1761 per c04.

answers.quote: Burhanul-Mulk Sa‘adat Khan was appointed subadar of Awadh in 1722. Burhanul-Mulk also held the combined offices of subadari, diwani and faujdari. In other words, he was responsible for managing the political, financial and military affairs of the province of Awadh.
answers.notes: Sa'adat Khan appointed subadar of Awadh in 1722 per c10.

answers.answer: নির্দিষ্ট অর্থের বিনিময়ে সর্বোচ্চ দরদাতার কাছে রাজস্ব আদায়ের ঠিকা দেওয়া
answers.quote: The state depended on local bankers and mahajans for loans. It sold the right to collect tax to the highest bidders. These “revenue farmers” (ijaradars) agreed to pay the state a fixed sum of money.
answers.notes: Tax collection sold to highest bidders (ijaradars) for a fixed sum per c11.

answers.quote: he transferred all Mughal jagirdars to Orissa and ordered a major reassessment of the revenues of Bengal. Revenue was collected in cash with great strictness from all zamindars.
answers.notes: Mughal jagirdars transferred to Orissa per c13.

answers.quote: was evident in Bengal under the rule of Alivardi Khan (r. 1740-1756). During his reign the banking house of Jagat Seth became extremely prosperous.
answers.notes: Banking house of Jagat Seth prospered under Alivardi Khan per c14.

answers.answer: বিজাপুরের পূর্ণকালীন নৌবাহিনী ছিল না এবং মুঘলদের নৌবাহিনীর ব্যবহারও ছিল খুব সীমিত
answers.quote: he felt the need to establish a navy. This was a truly revolutionary step at the time. By comparison, the Bijapur Sultanate (ruled by the Adil Shahi dynasty), maintained merchant ships but did not possess a full-time naval force which could protect the coast; even the Mughal Empire’s use of a navy was very limited. Thus, the Maratha Navy was born
answers.notes: Bijapur had no full-time naval force and Mughal navy use was very limited per c36.

answers.quote: To protect his people from powerful enemies, Chhatrapati Shivaji had recourse to the tactic of guerrilla warfare, which uses small groups of people in a focused way, with speed, surprise, and knowledge of the terrain to defeat bigger armies. There, Chhatrapati Shivaji killed Afzal Khan, and the Marathas, hidden in the mountains, routed the Khan’s army with guerrilla attacks.
answers.notes: Afzal Khan killed at the foot of Pratapgad fort per c37.

answers.quote: After Shivaji’s death, effective power in the Maratha state was wielded by a family of Chitpavan Brahmanas who served Shivaji’s successors as Peshwa (or principal minister). Poona became the capital of the Maratha kingdom.
answers.notes: Effective power with Chitpavan Brahmana Peshwa family per c23.

answers.answer: সমগ্র দাক্ষিণাত্য উপদ্বীপের অধিপতি, যাঁর চৌথ ও সরদেশমুখী আদায়ের অধিকার ছিল
answers.quote: Malwa and Gujarat were seized from the Mughals by the 1720s. By the 1730s, the Maratha king was recognised as the overlord of the entire Deccan peninsula. He possessed the right to levy chauth and sardeshmukhi in the entire region.
answers.notes: Maratha king recognised as overlord of entire Deccan peninsula by 1730s per c25.

answers.answer: বিশ্বাস রাও ও সদাশিব রাও ভাউ
answers.quote: 28,000 Marathas died on the battlefield, along with the commanders of the army, the Peshwa, minor son Vishwas Rao and the latter’s cousin, Sadashiv Rao Bhau. The Peshwa, Balaji Baji Rao did not survive for long, after hearing the tragic news of the defeat.
answers.notes: Vishwas Rao and Sadashiv Rao Bhau died at Panipat per c51.

answers.quote: Madhav Rao, who became Peshwa in 1761, was successful in subduing once again the old enemies, the Rohilas, the Rajput and Jat Chiefs in the north and Mysore and Hyderabad in the south.
answers.notes: Madhav Rao became Peshwa in 1761 and restored Maratha power per c53.

answers.quote: the Sikhs organized themselves into a number of bands called jathas, and later on misls. Their combined forces were known as the grand army (dal khalsa). A system called rakhi was introduced, offering protection to cultivators on the payment of a tax of 20 per cent of the produce.
answers.notes: Rakhi charged 20 per cent of produce per c20.

answers.quote: Churaman and Badan Singh founded the Jat State at Bharatpur but it was Suraj Mal who consolidated Jat power during his rule from 1756 to 1763.
answers.notes: Suraj Mal consolidated Jat power per c56.

answers.answer: ইংরেজ সৈন্যদের মাদ্রাজের পাঁচ মাইলের মধ্যে তাড়িয়ে নিয়ে গিয়ে চুক্তি আদায় করেন
answers.quote: His greatest moment of triumph was when he chased the English troops within five miles of Madras and dictated a treaty in 1769.
answers.notes: Haidar Ali chased English within five miles of Madras and dictated a treaty in 1769 per c61.

answers.answer: ফররুখ সিয়ার ও দ্বিতীয় আলমগীর নিহত হন; আহমদ শাহ ও দ্বিতীয় শাহ আলম অন্ধ হন
answers.quote: two Mughal emperors, Farrukh Siyar (1713-1719) and Alamgir II (1754-1759) were assassinated, and two others Ahmad Shah (1748-1754) and Shah Alam II (1759-1816) were blinded by their nobles.
answers.notes: Matches c05 exactly.

answers.answer: ১৭২৪ সালে, প্রতিদ্বন্দ্বী মুঘল-নিযুক্ত প্রার্থীকে যুদ্ধে হারিয়ে
answers.quote: Nizam Asaf Jah was first appointed a subadar (in charge of province) by the Mughal emperor in 1713 . But only after a military victory over his rival Mughal appointee in 1724 that he could take effective charge of the Deccan. He also assumed the right of making treaties, wars and granting mansabs and titles.
answers.notes: Effective charge of Deccan only after military victory over rival appointee in 1724 per c60.

answers.answer: চন্দননগর ও কলকাতার কুঠিতে দুর্গ নির্মাণের অনুমতি দেওয়া হয়নি
answers.quote: The Bengal rulers did not discriminate on religious grounds in making public appointments and Hindus reached high positions in the Civil Service. Fortifications were rightly not allowed in the French and English factories at Chandernagar and Calcutta
answers.notes: Fortifications not allowed at Chandernagore and Calcutta factories per c42.

answers.quote: Shivaji (1627-1680) carved out a stable kingdom with the support of powerful warrior families (deshmukhs). Groups of highly mobile, peasantpastoralists (kunbis) provided the backbone of the Maratha army.
answers.notes: Kunbi peasant-pastoralists were the backbone of the Maratha army per c22.

answers.answer: তিনি মালওয়া ও গুজরাট অধিকার করেন এবং নিজামকে দুবার চূড়ান্তভাবে হারান
answers.quote: Baji Rao himself led military campaigns and acquired the prosperous area of Malwa and Gujarat among others. The Nizam was decisively beaten twice by Baji Rao’s forces
answers.notes: Baji Rao acquired Malwa and Gujarat; Nizam decisively beaten twice per c47.

answers.answer: কোনো এলাকার চৌথ ও সরদেশমুখী আদায়ের দায়িত্ব ও বিজয়ের অনুমতি থেকে পাওয়া সামরিক-আর্থিক সুবিধা
answers.quote: Collection of Chauth and Sardeshmukhi of a certain area was assigned to the chiefs and conquest permitted.
answers.notes: Chiefs accepted Peshwa's authority for military/financial benefit; chauth/sardeshmukhi collection assigned to them per c46.

answers.answer: রোহিলখণ্ডের সর্দার ও অযোধ্যার নবাব আবদালির পক্ষ নেন; জাট-রাজপুতরাও বিচ্ছিন্ন ছিলেন
answers.quote: The Rohilkhand chief and the Awadh Nawabs, whose area had been overrun by the Marathas, even went to the extent of joining hands with Abdali. The Maratha armies marched alone to the battlefield of Panipat to confront Abdali.
answers.notes: Rohilkhand chief and Awadh Nawab joined Abdali (c50); Jat and Rajput chiefs alienated (c66).

answers.quote: The third battle of Panipat proved significant in the struggle for mastery over India. The Marathas’ ambition of replacing the Mughals as the imperial power was checked at a strategic point by this defeat. The beneficiaries were the British rather than the Afghas.
answers.notes: Beneficiaries were the British rather than the Afghans per c52.

answers.answer: ১৭৯৯ সালে; এরপর তিনি সার্বভৌম শিখ রাজতন্ত্রের ভিত্তি গড়েন
answers.quote: Ranjit Singh was the son of the Sukerchakia Misl Chief, Mahan Singh. He in alliance with Sahib Singh of Gujarat and Milkha Singh of Pindiwala, attacked Shahanchi Khan and occupied Lahore in 1799. After Lahore Ranjit Singh annexed Amritsar from the Bhangis along with all their other territories. Master of Lahore and Amritsar. Ranjit Singh, laid the foundation of a sovereign Sikh monarchy in the Punjab
answers.notes: Ranjit Singh occupied Lahore in 1799 and laid foundation of sovereign Sikh monarchy per c64.

answers.answer: লুণ্ঠনের ভাগের বদলে সৈন্যদের নিয়মিত বেতন, যাতে সেনাবাহিনীতে স্বার্থান্বেষী গোষ্ঠী গড়ে না ওঠে
answers.quote: by insisting to pay a regular salary to his troops rather than pay them with spoils of war, Tipu was able to ensure that no vested interest could emerge in the army. There was an attempt to induce organizational discipline more strongly along European lines. For this French soldiers were recruited and used for training special troops.
answers.notes: Tipu paid regular salary rather than spoils so no vested interest emerged per c62.

answers.quote: Murshid Kuli Khan became Governor of Bengal in 1717 under Mughal aegis but his link with Delhi was limited to sending tribute. Shuja-un-din became Nawab in 1727 and ruled till 1739 when Alivardi Khan assumed charge. In 1756 Siraj-ud-daula became the Nawab of Bengal on the death of his grandfather Alivardi Khan.
answers.notes: Both statements match c41 (Shuja-ud-din 1727-1739; Siraj succeeded grandfather Alivardi in 1756).

answers.quote: This allowed Maratha chiefs (sardars) like Sindhia of Gwalior, Gaekwad of Baroda and Bhonsle of Nagpur the resources to raise powerful armies. Ujjain expanded under Sindhia’s patronage and Indore under Holkar’s.
answers.notes: Sindhia-Gwalior, Gaekwad-Baroda, Bhonsle-Nagpur (c29); Indore under Holkar (c29).

answers.quote: Murshid Kuli Khan became Governor of Bengal in 1717 under Mughal aegis but his link with Delhi was limited to sending tribute. Shuja-un-din became Nawab in 1727 and ruled till 1739 when Alivardi Khan assumed charge. In 1756 Siraj-ud-daula became the Nawab of Bengal on the death of his grandfather Alivardi Khan.
answers.notes: Order: Murshid Quli (1717), Shuja-ud-din (1727), Alivardi (1740), Siraj (1756) per c41/c14.

answers.answer: A ও R দুটোই সঠিক এবং R হল A-এর সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা
answers.quote: The Rohilkhand chief and the Awadh Nawabs, whose area had been overrun by the Marathas, even went to the extent of joining hands with Abdali. The Maratha armies marched alone to the battlefield of Panipat to confront Abdali.
answers.notes: Marathas marched alone (c50); alienation of Jats/Rajputs (c66) and Rohilkhand/Awadh joining Abdali (c50) explain it.

answers.quote: Sawai Raja Jai Singh founded his new capital at Jaipur and was given the subadari of Agra in 1722.
answers.notes: Pair 4 is wrong: Sawai Jai Singh founded Jaipur (c17), not Udaipur. Pairs 1 (c19), 2 (c21), 3 (c30/c56) are correct.

answers.quote: Although extremely powerful and quite independent, the rulers of these states did not break their formal ties with the Mughal emperor.
answers.notes: Statement 1 per c67; statement 2 per c07.

answers.quote: 1657: Founding of the Maratha navy. 1666: Imprisonment at, and escape from, Agra. 1682–1707: Mughal-Maratha wars.
answers.notes: Birth (1630, c33), navy founded 1657 and Agra escape 1666 (c38), coronation 1674 (c35).
